insights.headline: Gold heads for a weekly loss as December Fed-hike bets harden; Brent tops $110.
insights.summary: Spot gold eased to about $4,165 on Friday and was headed for a 0.7% weekly loss as traders priced a 90% chance of a December Fed rate hike after hotter-than-expected US inflation data, with December COMEX futures settling near $4,181. Brent crude topped $110 a barrel for the first time since May on supply risks, keeping inflation-hedge demand in focus. In India, MCX gold futures reclaimed Rs 1.48 lakh per 10 grams and silver crossed Rs 2.13 lakh per kg, while the RBI fixed the SGB 2020-21 Series VII premature redemption price at Rs 14,614 ahead of the October 19 window.
points: Fed: CME FedWatch shows 90% odds of a December hike; Goolsbee called the hot PPI print 'discouraging'. Capital Economics sees gold edging lower into year-end.
Oil shock: Brent's first $110 print since May came as Houthi strikes and Russia-Ukraine energy attacks kept supply risk high; crude is up over 75% in 2026.
India physical: gold traded at a premium for the first time in 3+ months as the price pullback lifted jewellery buying ahead of Diwali.
Silver fell 0.7% to $57.05; gold FoFs halted fresh inflows before Diwali as record prices stretched retail demand.
Levels: FXEmpire flags $4,226 as the decisive ceiling for a bullish gold reversal after gold stalled in the $4,160-$4,180 band.

trending.title: A hawkish Fed is capping gold's week
trending.summary: Hot US inflation data pushed December-hike odds to 90%, and gold is trading as an inverse of real yields. Analysts see the metal rangebound, tilted to lower support, with $4,226 the ceiling to beat.

trending.title: India's physical market wakes up on the dip
trending.summary: Gold flipped to a premium in India for the first time in three months as lower prices pulled jewellery buyers back, while MCX futures reclaimed Rs 1.48 lakh/10g and silver crossed Rs 2.13 lakh/kg.

trending.title: $110 oil complicates the bullion picture
trending.summary: Brent's first $110 print since May has traders repricing inflation risk into bullion, though the same shock argues for a hawkish Fed. India's reserves fell $8.58 billion as the RBI absorbed the shock.

trending.title: Festive money takes stock of record prices
trending.summary: Gold FoFs halted fresh inflows before Diwali, the RBI fixed SGB Series VII redemption at Rs 14,614 (about 189% gains), and jewellers say this festive season is shaped by price, not footfall.

trending.title: Silver's two faces: macro drag, industrial bid
trending.summary: Silver slipped 0.7% to $57.05 with the macro drag, yet forecasts see it back above $57.50 on safe-haven demand even as analysts warn it keeps falling faster than gold on the way down.

items.title: Gold set for a weekly drop as traders assess Fed signals
items.summary: Spot gold eased to about $4,165/oz on Friday and was headed for a 0.7% weekly loss as traders weighed further Fed rate hikes after hotter-than-expected US inflation data; December COMEX futures settled near $4,181. CME FedWatch showed a 90% chance of a December hike. Reuters noted gold traded at a premium in India for the first time in three months as the pullback lifted jewellery buying.

items.title: Brent crude hits $110 a barrel for first time since May as supply concerns mount
items.summary: Brent crude rose 3.7% to $110 a barrel, its first print there since May, as Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and Russia-Ukraine energy attacks kept supply risks high. With crude up over 75% this year, traders are repricing inflation risk into bullion; the US offered 17 million barrels from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve.

items.title: India's forex reserves fall $8.58 billion to $726.03 billion: RBI
items.summary: The RBI's weekly data showed India's forex reserves fell $8.58 billion to $726.03 billion in the week ended October 9, following a $12.95 billion drop the week before. Gold reserves declined $1.32 billion to $105.09 billion and foreign currency assets fell $7.14 billion to $597.61 billion; reserves are down from September's record $785.71 billion high.

items.title: MCX Gold, Silver Surge Ahead On US Inflation Data, Crude Price Dip
items.summary: MCX gold futures rose by about ₹1,000 to reclaim levels above ₹1,48,000 per 10 grams, while silver moved up roughly ₹2,500 to top ₹2,13,000 per kilogram. Hotter-than-expected US CPI data kept Fed policy bets in flux — markets price a 72% chance of an October hold but 92% odds of a December hike — while spot gold held above $4,170 and silver traded near $57.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD rises above $57.50 amid safe-haven demand
items.summary: Silver extended gains for a second day to around $57.80 an ounce as an equity selloff drove safe-haven demand and bond yields fell. TD Securities noted "notable short-covering" by CTAs across rates, silver, platinum and palladium, easing systematic pressure; FedWatch pricing shows a 72% chance the Fed holds this month and a 92% chance of a December hike.

items.title: Gold FoFs halt fresh investments before Diwali: What investors can do
items.summary: About 17 fund houses including Mirae Asset, DSP and Tata have paused fresh lump-sum investments, switch-ins and new SIP/STP registrations into gold ETF funds-of-funds from 15-16 October on SEBI's direction, while existing SIPs, redemptions and direct ETF buying continue. September gold ETF inflows were Rs 4,451 crore.

items.title: RBI sets premature redemption price for Sovereign Gold Bond 2020-21 Series VII at ₹14,614
items.summary: The RBI fixed the premature redemption price for SGB 2020-21 Series VII at ₹14,614 per unit, due 19 October 2026 (20 Oct is a holiday). The price averages IBJA's 999-purity gold closes for Oct 14–16. Issued at ₹5,051 in Oct 2020, exiting now locks in ~189% gains over six years plus 2.5% annual interest.
points: Redemption price ₹14,614 per unit; due 19 Oct 2026 (20 Oct is a holiday).
Based on the simple average of IBJA 999 gold closing prices for Oct 14, 15 and 16.
Issued at ₹5,051 in Oct 2020 — exit implies ~189% capital gains over six years, plus 2.5% annual interest.
Premature redemption is allowed only on interest payment dates after five years from issue.

items.title: Gold, silver diverge as Fed-pause hopes collide with surging crude
items.summary: Spot gold held near $4,167.90 an ounce (-0.05%) while spot silver fell 0.78% to $56.85 in late Friday US trade. Brent settled at $109.86 and WTI topped $100, and rebounding yields offset a weaker dollar and safe-haven demand. US import prices rose 1.1% m/m and 8.1% y/y. After Chair Warsh gave no October signal, futures priced an 83% chance of no change on Oct 27-28.
points: Spot gold near $4,167.90 (-0.05%); spot silver near $56.85 (-0.78%) in late Friday US trade.
Brent settled at $109.86/bbl and WTI topped $100 as Gulf vessel attacks and Iran tensions intensified.
US import prices +1.1% m/m, +8.1% y/y — the largest annual rise since July 2022.
Futures price ~83% odds of no Fed change on Oct 27-28 after Warsh gave no hike signal; December hike bets persist.
10-year Treasury yield recovered toward 5.12%; the dollar index stayed under pressure.

items.title: India gold swings to premium as lower prices lift jewellery demand
items.summary: Dealers quoted premiums of up to $7 an ounce over official domestic prices this week — India's first premium in over three months — against discounts of up to $6 last week, as lower prices revived jewellery buying. Domestic gold sat near ₹148,200 per 10 grams Friday after a two-week low of ₹145,627. September imports collapsed to $1.8 billion from $9.6 billion a year earlier.

items.title: Why silver is falling faster than gold: What it means for the next surge
items.summary: CPM Group's Jeffrey Christian notes gold consolidating in a $4,050-$4,200 range while silver has broken below $60 to trade near $55.77, arguing silver's larger industrial-demand share and substitution pressure at high prices explain its steeper fall. He flags the risk of a sharper selloff being followed by strong investment demand and a decisive break above $4,200 for gold.

items.title: Gold (XAU/USD) Price Forecast: Bulls Face Crucial $4,226 Resistance
items.summary: FXEmpire's weekly technical read: gold formed a higher weekly high and higher low, hinting at an attempted reversal of the bearish correction. A decisive move above $4,226 would confirm a bullish daily reversal; until then, holding support above $4,066 stays central. A breakout would project an ABCD measured move toward $4,821.
points: Weekly higher high and higher low hint at a reversal attempt; no close yet above last week's $4,208 high (FXEmpire).
A decisive break above $4,226 confirms a bullish reversal; a rise above this week's $4,217 high signals renewed strength (FXEmpire).
Holding support above $4,066 is central; an ABCD pattern projects a measured move toward $4,821 on a breakout (FXEmpire).

items.title: Gold stuck near $4,160–$4,180 resistance as rising oil and yields cap the rebound
items.summary: FXEmpire's Vladimir Zernov: gold pulled back as traders focused on the oil rally (+3.5%) and rebounding yields — the 10-year topped 5.10% while the dollar weakened. Futures imply 17.2% October hike odds, but traders still price December/January hikes. Gold tests $4,160–$4,180 resistance (above $4,180 opens $4,300–$4,320); silver tests $56–$57; platinum flat near $1,600–$1,620.
points: Gold resistance at $4,160–$4,180; above $4,180 targets $4,300–$4,320 (FXEmpire technical view).
Oil +3.5% on US–Iran escalation fears; 10-year yield above 5.10% weighed on gold.
FedWatch: ~17% October hike odds; traders still price December/January hikes.
Silver testing $56–$57 support; platinum near $1,600–$1,620.

items.title: Gold vs silver vs platinum: Which metal saw biggest rally since last Dussehra? Experts explain outlook
items.summary: Silver is the standout since last Dussehra, up about 47% in rupee terms versus gold's ~26% and platinum's ~10.5%; the rupee's slide and the May duty rise to 15% lifted domestic returns. Silver swung wildly, up 155% by January and now 53% off its peak, so buyers near the top stay at a loss. Mint cites experts who see gold backed by central-bank buying, silver with higher upside but more volatility.

items.title: Titan, Senco Gold, Kalyan Jewellers, PC Jeweller: What makes this festive season different?
items.summary: Listed jewellers posted healthy Q2 FY27 growth — Titan jewellery +21% YoY, Kalyan India revenue +27%, Senco +31%, PC Jeweller consolidated +28% — though demand cooled late in the quarter as the festive calendar shifted into Q3. Jewellers remain upbeat on Diwali, Dhanteras and weddings, even as PM Modi's May 2026 appeal to defer gold buying and volatile prices keep volumes the key watch.
